gbm_population_evidence.quote: Evidence of recurrent HGG that in the opinion of the treating team does not represent pseudoprogression and would require surgical resection
High grade gliomas (WHO grade III and IV)(HGG) are the most common malignant, and aggressive brain tumour in humans.

gbm_population_flag.reason: Recurrent HGG (WHO grade III and IV) without explicit mention of glioblastoma anywhere in the record; grade IV would include GBM implicitly.

candidate_evidence.quote: targeting hexokinase 2 (HK2), the first committed step of glucose metabolism, with azole class drugs has been shown to display favourable anti-tumour effects in both in vitro and in vivo HGG models.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Evidence of recurrent HGG that in the opinion of the treating team does not represent pseudoprogression

role_evidence.quote: Ketoconazole (KCZ) Single Dose Group: Single dose 400mg oral tablets 4-24 hours prior to surgery
Posaconazole (PCZ) Single Dose group: Single dose 300 mg delayed release oral tablets 4-24 hours prior to surgery

source_quote.quote: Assess Hexokinase 2 activity: enzyme activity measured using optical absorbance with a spectrophotometer

coder_notes: Window-of-opportunity Phase 0 (EARLY_PHASE1) pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic study; separate KCZ and PCZ arms. Other tissue endpoints (glycolytic metabolites, Ki-67, TUNEL, VEGF/CD31 IHC) are pharmacodynamic/histological and not recorded as molecular biomarkers.
